title: How to Convert a $100,000 Salary Per Week to Hourly, Annual, Tax and Super
description: Learn how to convert a $100,000 salary per week to hourly and annual figures, including tax, super, and casual loading. Based on Fair Work and ATO data.
salarySummary: A $100,000 salary per week equates to $2,631.58 per hour for a 38-hour week and $5.2 million annually, before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert a weekly salary to an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Divide the weekly salary by the number of hours worked per week. For a standard 38-hour week, a $100,000 salary per week gives $100,000 ÷ 38 = $2,631.58 per hour. The same formula works for any weekly amount: hourly rate = weekly salary ÷ hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for award-free employees?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage for casual employees includes a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For award-free adult employees, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 plus 25%). This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For a $100,000 salary per week ($5.2 million annually), the super contribution would be 12% of that amount, but it is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026-27). Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost for the employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding a $100,000 Salary Per Week

If you come across a job offer or a contract that states a **$100,000 salary per week**, you might wonder what that means in terms of hourly pay, annual income, tax, and superannuation. While $100,000 per week is an exceptionally high figure (equivalent to $5.2 million per year), the same conversion principles apply to any weekly salary. This article walks you through the calculations using the standard 38-hour week, explains the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and super paid on top, and shows how to estimate your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual and Back

The core relationship is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

Conversely, to find the hourly rate from a weekly salary:

**Hourly rate = weekly salary ÷ hours per week**

For a **$100,000 salary per week** and a 38‑hour week:

- Hourly rate = $100,000 ÷ 38 = **$2,631.58 per hour**
- Annual gross = $100,000 × 52 = **$5,200,000**

This assumes you work every week of the year at the same rate, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The same formula works for any weekly amount – simply divide by your usual hours.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross:

**Fortnightly pay = weekly salary × 2**

For a $100,000 salary per week, that’s $200,000 per fortnight. Knowing your fortnightly figure helps with budgeting and comparing to typical payslips.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

Not everyone earns $100,000 per week. The Fair Work Commission sets the **National Minimum Wage** for award‑free employees. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is:

- **$26.44 per hour** (base rate)
- **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 ordinary hours

This is the floor. Most employees are covered by an award (industry or occupation‑specific) which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award – you can find your classification and corresponding rate using the [pay guides](/blog) tool.

### Casual Loading

If you work casually and are not covered by an award, the National Minimum Wage includes a **25% casual loading** on top of the base rate. That means:

- Casual minimum rate = $26.44 × 1.25 = **$33.05 per hour**
- Casual weekly minimum = $1,004.90 × 1.25 = **$1,256.13 per week**

The loading compensates for entitlements casuals don’t receive, such as paid sick leave and annual leave. On this site, when you enter your hourly rate, you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading – do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is **12% of ordinary earnings**, paid by your employer **on top** of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. For a $100,000 salary per week ($5.2 million annually), the super contribution would be 12% of that amount, but the **maximum contribution base** for 2026‑27 is **$270,830 per year**. That means super is capped at $270,830 × 12% = $32,499.60 per year, regardless of higher earnings. For most workers, super is simply 12% of their ordinary time earnings.

### Tax on a $100,000 Salary Per Week

For the 2026‑27 income year, Australian resident tax rates are:

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|----------------|-------------------|
| $0 – $18,200 | Nil |
| $18,201 – $45,000 | 15% for each $1 over $18,200 |
| $45,001 – $135,000 | $4,020 plus 30% for each $1 over $45,000 |
| $135,001 – $190,000 | $31,020 plus 37% for each $1 over $135,000 |
| $190,001+ | $51,370 plus 45% for each $1 over $190,000 |

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (based on 2025‑26 single reduction thresholds as 2026‑27 thresholds are not confirmed here).

For a $5.2 million annual income, the tax would be substantial – the top marginal rate of 45% applies to the vast majority. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

### Putting It All Together

Whether you’re looking at a **$100,000 salary per week** or a more typical figure, the steps are the same:

1. Determine your weekly or hourly base rate.
2. Multiply by 52 for annual gross (or divide by hours for hourly).
3. Add casual loading if applicable (25% on top).
4. Remember super is extra, paid by the employer.
5. Estimate tax using the resident scale and Medicare.

For award‑covered employees, always check the relevant pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has the latest national rates, and the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains contribution caps.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026‑27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025‑26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026‑27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
